conversation:
Patient: I'm 45 years old, male. I came in because I've been having pain in my right elbow for about a week. It started when I was playing lacrosse with my kids, and it hurts whenever I move it.
Doctor: Could you please confirm your age, gender, and describe the nature of the pain in your right elbow, including any specific activities that aggravate or relieve it?
Patient: I'm 45, male. The pain is sharp and happens anytime I move my elbow. It started when I was playing lacrosse with my kids, and my son hit me with the stick. It radiates down my forearm, and it's been hurting me ever since.
Doctor: Have you noticed any swelling, bruising, or restricted range of motion in your right elbow?
Patient: Yes, there's some swelling and a little bruising around the tip of my elbow, and it's pretty painful when I try to move it. The pain radiates down my forearm, and I can't really bend or straighten it without discomfort.
Doctor: Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your hand or fingers since the injury?
Patient: No, I haven't had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my hand or fingers since the injury. The pain is mainly in my elbow and forearm, and I can still move my hand and fingers, though it's uncomfortable.
Doctor: Have you experienced any previous elbow injuries or conditions, such as fractures, dislocations, or ligament tears?
Patient: No, I don't think I've had any previous elbow injuries or conditions like fractures, dislocations, or ligament tears. This is the first time I've had pain like this in my elbow.
Doctor: Can you specify the exact location of the pain in your elbow (e.g., on the outside, inside, or back of the elbow)?
Patient: The pain is right at the tip of my elbow, on the back side, and it radiates down my forearm. It's really sharp whenever I move it.
Doctor: Have you had any imaging studies, such as X-rays or an MRI, performed for this injury?
Patient: No, I haven't had any imaging studies done for this injury yet. The doctor mentioned they did an X-ray before I came in, and it was normal, but I didn't get to see the results myself.
Doctor: Did the X-ray results confirm any fractures or dislocations in the right elbow?
Patient: No, the X-ray results didn't show any fractures or dislocations in the right elbow. The doctor said the X-ray was normal, so there's nothing broken.
Doctor: Have you undergone any MRI or ultrasound imaging of the right elbow to evaluate for soft tissue injuries, ligamentous damage, or tendonitis?
Patient: No, I haven't had any MRI or ultrasound imaging of the right elbow. The doctor mentioned they did an X-ray before I came in, and it was normal, but there was no mention of any other imaging like an MRI or ultrasound.
Doctor: Have you noticed any specific activities or movements that make the pain worse or better? For example, does lifting objects, bending your elbow, or straightening it cause more discomfort?
Patient: Yes, the pain gets worse whenever I move my elbow, especially when I flex or extend it. Lifting objects or trying to straighten my arm really aggravates it, and it's pretty sharp every time I do that.
Doctor: Has the patient undergone any physical therapy or received any treatment for the elbow pain since the injury?
Patient: No, I haven't had any physical therapy or treatment for the elbow pain since the injury. I tried taking some Advil a couple of days ago, and it helped a little, but I usually just forget about it. I haven’t done anything else for it.
Doctor: Has the patient experienced any locking, clicking, or popping sensations in the elbow when moving it?
Patient: No, I haven't experienced any locking, clicking, or popping sensations in the elbow when moving it. It just hurts when I move it, especially when flexing or extending, and it radiates down my forearm.
Doctor: Has the patient noticed any changes in the strength of the arm or hand, or any difficulty gripping objects?
Patient: No, I haven't noticed any changes in the strength of my arm or hand, and I don't have any difficulty gripping objects. The main issue is the pain when I move my elbow, which radiates down my forearm. I haven't had any trouble with my grip or strength.
Doctor: Has the patient experienced any locking, clicking, or popping sensations in the elbow during movement?
Patient: No, I haven't experienced any locking, clicking, or popping sensations in the elbow during movement. It just hurts when I move it, especially when flexing or extending, and it radiates down my forearm.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies such as an MRI or ultrasound for the right elbow, and if so, what were the findings?
Patient: No, I haven't undergone any imaging studies such as an MRI or ultrasound for the right elbow. The doctor mentioned that an x-ray was done before I came in, and it showed nothing broken or abnormal, so I don’t have any other imaging results.
